then.u_message: <global_val:pf_say_a> spots you first.  "Look who it is."  You've been gone <global_val:pf_aw_gone_t>.
<global_val:pf_say_a> sees you coming and walks the last bit of the way out to meet you.  "There you are.  Gone <global_val:pf_aw_gone_t>, and not a word.  We were starting to talk about you."
<global_val:pf_say_a> just looks at you for a long moment.  "We'd started to think you weren't coming back."  You've been gone <global_val:pf_aw_gone_t>.
Nobody makes a fuss.  The place got on without you for <global_val:pf_aw_gone_t>.
There's food at home: what the place put by while you were gone, set aside for you.
<global_val:pf_aw_wm_a> and <global_val:pf_aw_wm_b> spent the evenings together while you were gone.  It shows.
<global_val:pf_aw_tn_a> and <global_val:pf_aw_tn_b> had words more than once while you were gone.  Everyone has an opinion about it.
<global_val:pf_aw_mt_a> and <global_val:pf_aw_mt_b> got to know each other a little while you were gone.
<global_val:pf_say_a> has a bandage on one arm and a story about the night the raiders came.  They tell it twice before supper.
There's a meeting tonight, now that you're back.  The last one waited for you.
On <global_val:pf_aw_meet_dwhen>, <global_val:pf_chief_name> held the meeting without you.  You hear how it went:
<global_val:pf_aw_dead_name>'s grave is behind the place: fresh earth, and a marker with the name scratched in.  Someone has left flowers.
They buried <global_val:pf_aw_dead_name> while you were gone.  People keep starting to say the name and stopping.
